items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I knew I was a member of the Onward Brass Band, Manuel Perez... I worked with him on the Roof Garden... We had Emmanuel Perez, Buddy Johnson, myself...

ctx.x: I was waiting for the railroad there and got my job waiting for the railroad there. So you stayed out there there? A while.

I stayed out there from 19 from October. I must have got in Los Angeles from 1919 by October the first or second. And it was the funnest thing when I got off the train I had on a straw hat in October. And I guess the people out there was looking at me, you know, well it was hot just like it is this year when I left. And we got off the train I had a straw hat on. I felt so embarrassed and ashamed. That's a warm air chair though. Yes indeed, having a straw hat on. We played at the Cadillac in Los Angeles, I guess…
Yes, he told us something about the date.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: When I was playing with him, there were Maurice, Manuel Perez, and that sometime Rick.

ctx.x: Oh. Who were the three tracks with the Arnold one? I couldn't get that.

That's the Arnold man. When I was playing with him. Mm-hmm. When I was playing with him, there were Maurice, Manuel Perez, and that sometime Rick. Mm-hmm. And sometime another trumpet player. Uh-huh. But Maurice and Manuel was the main trumpet players. Mm-hmm. And, uh, Eddie Yank on trombone. Yank Johnson on trombone. And Piku played with us. Uh-huh. And sometime Eddie Sherry playing that. Had old man Tatt baritone. Mm-hmm. And who else was playing trombone with the Ancret to trombone? Well, I'm afraid. I never…

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Of course, Celestine always read music, just like Manuel Perez, you see.

ctx.x: Then they'd pick up a, oh, man, I swear to God, that people played so long, man. Oh, man.

Now, the only time they would play short, they'd play orchestration, you see. Well, they'd play it down. And if it was a good orchestration, you know, that they liked, well, they'd go back to the chorus and play one or two, you see. Of course, Celestine always read music, just like Manuel Perez, you see. Always had musicians in their reach, you know. It felt like Buddy Pettine, you know.

You know, when I used to go out to Tyler's Beer Garden? Who? To Tyler's Beer Garden during the war. I don't think you were ever out there. No, I don't. But Joe Avery and Wilbur Tillman had the band. Tillman played with us?
